item.title: Things I learned this week
item.description:
Every week I keep a running list of “huh, didn’t know that” moments. Most of them are small. Here’s this week’s, in the order I bumped into them.

Hugo output formats don’t hot-reload

If you add a new output format to hugo.toml, the dev server won’t pick it up live. You have to restart hugo server. I spent fifteen minutes wondering why /llms.txt was 404ing before I remembered that.

safeJS is required for JSON-LD

Go’s html/template will happily JS-escape the JSON you put inside a <script> tag, turning your object into a quoted string. You have to pipe through safeJS after jsonify so the runtime treats the output as already-safe JavaScript.

item.title: A short note on naming things
item.description:
The longer I write code, the more I think the best names are the ones nobody will quote at a conference. count, result, item. Short, accurate, forgettable. The reader’s attention is finite, and every clever name spends some of it.

Save the inventive names for the places where the concept is genuinely new — a module, a public function, a domain term. Inside a function, you almost never need a thesaurus. You need a noun and a context, and the context is the function itself.

item.title: WebGL with three.js
item.description:
This is an example post demonstrating the new frontmatter structure compatible with Jekyll posts.

Features Demonstrated

This post shows how the Hugo theme now supports:

  • description: A description field that appears in both the post and listings
  • canonical: Link to the original publication URL
  • category: Post categorization
  • tags: Multiple tags for organizing content
  • assets: Arrays for page-specific CSS and JavaScript files

Assets Array
